words.dictionaryUrdu: كَذَّبَ کا مطلب کسی کو جھوٹا کہنا یا کسی بات کو جھٹلانا ہے۔ یہاں نعمتوں کا انکار مراد ہے؛ اسے مجرد كَذَبَ یعنی جھوٹ بولنے سے الگ سمجھیں۔
words.verbNoteUrdu: كَذَّبَ، يُكَذِّبُ بابِ تفعیل سے یہ مخاطب تثنیہ کا معروف مضارع ہے؛ کوئی ناصب یا جازم نہیں، اس لیے نون برقرار ہے۔ الف دونوں مخاطب جماعتوں کا فاعل ہے؛ مفعولی ضمیر متصل نہیں۔

auditNotes.noteEnglish: Raw QAC labels the verb and its subject suffix 2FD. The antecedent is the third-person feminine dual noun for the two springs; the reviewed lexeme explicitly confirms 3FD. Authored as third-person feminine dual indicative active, with retained nun.

Raw word-level QAC labels the noun genitive and wa conjunctive. Followed the explicit ayah grammar note: wa introduces a circumstantial nominal clause, jana is nominative mubtada with implied damma on alif, and dan is its predicate.

Raw QAC morphology and generated word-level irab label the dual accusative. It is the genitive mudaf ilayh of jana in the nominal clause, as required by the ayah-level analysis and the rule library; ya marks genitive here.
At 55:51:1, 55:53:1 and 55:55:1 raw QAC calls ayy a generic noun, unlike INTG at 55:49:1. All are interrogative nouns in the identical rhetorical question; the derived noun POS is retained.
For the repeated refrain followed the supplied word-level irab treating fa as resumptive. An implied-condition/answer analysis is possible, but is not asserted in these lessons.
For the repeated plural ala, used the root library singular ala (أَلًى) as lemma and mentioned the alternative ila (إِلًى) in dictionary notes; the plural itself is the usual lexical citation.

QAC labels the broken plural bataain masculine plural although its singular bitana is feminine. The lesson states broken plural without asserting that gender label and retains the feminine singular possessive suffix referring to nonhuman plural bedding.
